ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a large triangle SZU. Point Y is on side SZ, and sides SY and YZ have the same single tick mark, indicating that Y is the midpoint of SZ; point T is on side SU, and ST and TU have the same triple tick marks, indicating that T is the midpoint of SU; point V is on side ZU, and ZV and VU have the same double tick marks, indicating that V is the midpoint of ZU. The figure shows the three line segments UY, SV, and ZT, which intersect at point J. The problem gives UJ=9, VJ=3, ZT=18. Reasoning: Because Y, T, and V are respectively the midpoints of the three sides of triangle SZU, UY, ZT, and SV are the three medians of triangle SZU, and they intersect at point J, so J is the centroid of the triangle. The centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio in the direction from the vertex to the midpoint. On the median segment ZT, ZJ is the part from vertex Z to centroid J, so ZJ = (2/3)ZT = (2/3)×18 = 12.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as triangle SZU with midpoint markings: Y is the midpoint of SZ, V is the midpoint of ZU, and T is the midpoint of SU. Treat the diagram algebraically with position vectors for S, Z, and U. Since T is the midpoint of SU, T = (S + U)/2. Since J lies at the common intersection of medians, equivalently solve the median-intersection position: J = (S + Z + U)/3. Compare J with the point on segment ZT: points on ZT have form Z + lambda(T - Z). Substituting T = (S + U)/2 gives J = Z + (2/3)(T - Z), so J is two-thirds of the way from Z to T. From the text ZT = 18, hence ZJ = (2/3)·18 = 12.
